reply_text:
Your four icons aren't among the 20 chips the page has, so I'm looking for them on the original ChipWits IBOL sheet.Your four icons are on the original sheet's operator palette. I'm cutting them out at the same size as the existing chips.I've cut three chips. The roller skate is clipped on the left, so I'm redoing that one before wiring them into the legend.㊥ Gist: The legend now shows the roller skate for explore, the door for withdraw and the loop arrow for gist. All three are on the published turns page (futon3 `7ab5e2a`). Explore notes in the feed itself also get the skate now. I've left retract without a chip, because I couldn't find an earlier assignment to an X-and-up-arrow icon. In `ibol_verbs.json`, "retract" is one of the verbs listed under DECREMENT (the minus chip), with disagree. Which icon do you mean? Also, which icon are you worried about? The new rows had no chip before this, so I can't tell which "other icon" you mean.

㊢ (where the chips came from) The page's 20 chips didn't include any of these, so I cut them from `chipwits-forth/mac/graphics/IBOL_Graphics.png`. That's the same sheet the existing chips match: op-plus is found there pixel for pixel. They're in the same format as the others, black on transparent and 15 pixels wide. They're named `op-move`, `op-door` and `op-loop`, and they sit in the published `chips/` directory next to the others. Like the other chips, they're not in any repo.

㊬ (what I checked)
- **Rendering:** I rendered `feed.html` in headless Chromium. All three images load (HTTP 200), and op-move appears 18 times, once in the legend and on explore notes in the feed.
- **Gates:** clj-kondo and the parens check are clean, and the release build has 0 warnings.

㊟ (labels not checked) I've labelled the rows ROLLER SKATE, DOOR and LOOP ARROW, after how they look, and left the "IBOL says" line empty. I haven't checked what these chips do in ChipWits against the manual, so their real operator names may differ. The manual PDFs are in `chipwits-forth/docs` if you want the rows to give the IBOL meaning.

previous_reply_acts.text: Gist: I've asked codex-10 to build the War Machine's version of the table: one row per act a click actually performs, with loop stage, R-node, the nearest of the 23 intents or "none", and whether the act is addressed to you. The legend went along as the reference. The table goes in a typed EDN file in futon2. Wiring it into click run-time reporting is a separate, later job. The mission gets an unchecked item for that, which is met when a click receipt lists its acts by the table's ids.

(the handoff)
- **Job:** `invoke-1790876966037-29768-66595380`, in work mode. It's running, and codex-10 was idle beforehand.
- **Park:** `park-96f8f5ef-2978-4865-b928-3303c30ea3c2`, with a 45-minute deadline.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (why the packet is shaped this way) Since WM acts are mostly not linguistic, I told codex-10 to enumerate them from code and recent click receipts, not from design docs. I also told it not to force an intent onto an act: a "none" row tells us where the operator vocabulary doesn't reach. The column for "addressed to the operator" is the one M-aif-over-the-operator needs. Those are the acts that would become offers, such as the nag, brief and silent notifications behind WR-0.
